CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Stephanie Morales is a 36-year-old female presenting with left ankle pain. Two days ago, the patient slipped on snow and ice while walking to her car. Her left ankle twisted and turned underneath her, with pain localized to the outside/lateral aspect of the ankle. She fell and was able to get up on her own, though it was very sore. Since the incident, she has developed significant swelling and pain, making it difficult to walk. She has attempted ibuprofen, ice, and elevation with some improvement. Pain is localized to the outside of her ankle with no involvement of the calf, lower leg, or knee. She denies bleeding but confirms visible swelling.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies pain above the ankle, in the calf, lower leg, or knee. Denies bleeding.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - well-controlled on metformin
2. Hypertension
3. Systolic ejection murmur - unchanged from prior visits

MEDICATIONS
1. Metformin
2. Norvasc
3. Ibuprofen (patient-initiated)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is active and exercises regularly. Follows diabetic diet with reduction of sweets and sugars. Regularly checks blood glucose levels.

Vital Signs: Blood pressure 120/70 mmHg
Neck: Normal, no bruits
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Heart: Normal, 2/6 systolic ejection murmur noted (unchanged from prior)

RESULTS

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left ankle sprain with suspected fracture rule-out
   - X-ray of left ankle ordered due to tenderness over lateral malleolus and fifth metatarsal
   - Air splint applied
   - Crutches provided
   - Avoid weightbearing until x-ray reviewed
   - Naproxen 500 mg twice daily for pain control
   - Continue ice and elevation
   - Will call patient with x-ray results; if fracture present, will refer to orthopedics
   - If negative, will discontinue air splint and progress to partial weightbearing as tolerated

2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
   - Continue metformin
   - Keep scheduled ophthalmology appointment in next couple of weeks
   - Hemoglobin A1C ordered today
   - Baseline laboratory studies ordered

3. Hypertension

   - Continue current management
